samples.summary: Unvalidated persisted `spillRows`/`spillCols` now drive an unbounded per-cell scan on every document open and undo/redo (`loadSpillBlockers` → `findSpillBlocker`), giving any collaborator a persistent client-side DoS
samples.evidence: `loadSpillBlockers` (sheet.ts:1039-1051) reads every formula cell from the store and passes the *stored* `cell.spillRows`/`cell.spillCols` straight into `findSpillBlocker` (sheet.ts:1011-1029), which loops `rows*cols` times with an `await this.getCell(...)` per iteration and only exits early if it finds a blocker. Those fields are attacker-controlled data, not locally computed values: `YorkieStore.getFormulaGrid` (packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-store.ts:549-558) returns doc cells with a bare `cell as Cell` cast, `worksheetEntries`/`getWorksheetEntries` (packages/sheets/src/model/workbook/worksheet-grid.ts:145-168) copy the cell object verbatim, the yorkie-store write path only checks `!== undefined` before copying `spillRows`/`spillCols` (yorkie-store.ts:231-236), and no backend validation of these fields exists (grep for `spillRows` in packages/backend/src returns nothing). Attack: a user with edit access to a shared doc (or any crafted Yorkie/API write) sets one cell to `{f:'=1', spillBlocked:true, spillRows:1e9, spillCols:1e9}` over empty space. `Worksheet.initialize` now calls `await this.sheet.loadSpillBlockers()` unconditionally (packages/sheets/src/view/worksheet.ts, added after `loadMerges`), so every subsequent viewer — including the owner and read-only viewers — hangs the tab before the grid ever renders, and `Sheet.undo`/`redo` re-trigger the same loop. Before this change nothing on the open path iterated persisted spill footprints (the pre-existing loops in calculator.ts:74-85 only ran for a cell being recalculated), so the change turns a gesture-scoped hazard into a document-open denial of service with no bound, no clamp against sheet dimensions, and no cap on total work across cells.

samples.summary: `clearCellForOverwrite` feeds an untrusted stored `spillAnchor` string into the recalculation path, where `parseRef` throws on a malformed value and aborts the merge/move mid-mutation
samples.evidence: `clearCellForOverwrite` does `requeuedAnchors.add(cell.spillAnchor)` (sheet.ts:1078) using the raw string from the store; `recalculateWithUnblocked` (sheet.ts:1116-1135) inserts it into the changed set and the dependants map, and `calculate` then executes `const ref = parseRef(sref)` with no try/catch (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/calculator.ts:48). `parseRef` throws `new Error('Invalid Reference')` for any string without a leading column label (packages/sheets/src/model/core/coordinates.ts:336-351), and `spillAnchor` is copied verbatim out of the CRDT document (yorkie-store.ts:228-230, worksheet-grid.ts:145-168) with no validation client- or server-side. Attack: a collaborator writes `{v:'x', spillAnchor:'@@'}` into a cell; the next user who merges or drag-moves a range covering it hits the throw inside the `beginBatch`/`endBatch` block of `mergeSelection` (sheet.ts:~4603) or `moveRangeTo`, so the gesture rejects after part of the clearing loop has already committed (unhandled rejection in the view handler). Previously these paths explicitly skipped cells with a `spillAnchor` (`if (cell.spillAnchor) continue;` in the code this diff replaced), so the untrusted value never reached `parseRef` from here. Impact is limited to an aborted gesture / partially applied merge rather than data disclosure, hence minor; I did not build a running exploit, hence low confidence.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo: `findSpillBlocker` (sheet.ts:1011-1029) runs a `rows*cols` loop with an awaited `getCell` per iteration and no clamp to sheet dimensions (`getCell` at sheet.ts:946-948 does no bounds checking, so out-of-range refs never terminate the loop). `loadSpillBlockers` (sheet.ts:1039-1051) feeds it the *stored* `cell.spillRows`/`cell.spillCols` with only a truthiness guard at sheet.ts:1043, and is called unconditionally on document open (view/worksheet.ts:424, inside `initialize` before `render()`) and on undo/redo (sheet.ts:5103, 5140). Those fields are untrusted persisted data: yorkie-store.ts:549-558 returns doc cells via a bare `cell as Cell` cast, worksheet-grid.ts:145-168 copies stored cells verbatim, the write path only checks `!== undefined` (yorkie-store.ts:231-236), and a grep for `spillRows` across packages/sheets/src and `spill` across packages/backend/src shows no validation or clamping on any layer. A collaborator (or crafted Yorkie/API write) persisting spillRows/spillCols of ~1e9 with `spillBlocked:true` over empty space hangs every subsequent viewer's tab before render. No guard elsewhere makes this unreachable, and unvalidated attacker-controlled input driving unbounded work is within the unsafe-input-handling lane, so no named refutation ground applies.
